source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Move complex IV preparation to the bedside because uncontrolled environments reduce calculation and contamination errors.","B":"Eliminate pharmacist verification for compounded sterile products because centralized preparation makes review unnecessary.","C":"Use centralized preparation mainly to delay administration, because specialized facilities provide little safety advantage.","D":"Use trained pharmacy staff, controlled environments, and verification systems to reduce compounding and preparation risk."}}
source_row.rationale: Centralized sterile compounding uses trained personnel, controlled environments, standard procedures and verification to reduce preparation and contamination risk compared with unnecessary complex bedside compounding.
source_row.source_detail: ASHP sterile compounding resources emphasize compliance with USP standards, controlled environments, trained personnel, standardized processes and medication-safety safeguards for compounded sterile preparations. Current ASHP compounding practice resources rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Why are many complex sterile IV admixtures prepared in a centralized pharmacy compounding area rather than at the bedside?
